turns.response_html:
It looks like you've run into a classic compatibility issue between different butane standards. The cartridge on the left appears to be a cassette-style gas canister (often used for portable camping stoves), while the torch on the right is designed for a standard refined butane refill typically found in smaller aerosol-style cans.

To bridge this gap safely and get that torch filled, you have a few options:

1. The Adapter Solution

You can purchase a "Cassette to Lindal" or "Butane Canister Adapter." These are small plastic or metal fittings that snap onto the collar of the large silver canister. They feature a narrow needle-thin nozzle on the other end that will fit the brass receiver of your torch.

  • What to look for: Search for "Butane refill adapter for camping gas" or "Cassette gas refill nozzle."

2. Check the Canister Cap

Before buying anything, check the plastic cap that came with the silver butane canister. Some manufacturers include a multi-tip adapter set hidden inside the lid. It usually looks like a small plastic "tree" with several different sized nozzles you can break off and press onto the main stem.

3. Use the Correct Fuel Type

While they both contain butane, there is a reason for the different nozzles:

  • Camping Butane (Left): Often contains a mix of butane and propane and may have more impurities.
  • Lighter/Torch Butane (Right): Usually labeled "3x Refined" or "5x Refined." Using "dirty" gas from a stove canister can eventually clog the tiny internal jets of a high-performance torch.

Safety Warning

When attempting a refill with an adapter, ensure you are in a well-ventilated area away from any open flames. If you hear a significant hissing sound or feel liquid gas on your hands, stop immediately; the seal isn't tight enough, and you risk a flash fire.
